title: Hacienda Luisita Inc. v. Presidential Agrarian Reform Council
summary: The Supreme Court revoked the Stock Distribution Option Agreement (SDOA) of Hacienda Luisita and ordered the compulsory acquisition and distribution of the hacienda lands to qualified farmworker-beneficiaries. The SDOA was found to have failed in its purpose of benefiting the farmers.
doctrine: The Stock Distribution Option under Section 31 of RA 6657 requires that the farmworkers genuinely benefit from the arrangement. When the SDO fails to achieve its purpose and the farmworkers are not better off than they were before, the PARC may revoke the SDO and order compulsory land distribution.
fullText:
VELASCO, JR., J.:

The constitutionality and legality of the Stock Distribution Option Agreement of Hacienda Luisita is the central issue in this case.

Section 31 of RA 6657 provides an alternative to the outright transfer of land ownership through a stock distribution option where the farm workers receive shares of stock in the corporation that owns the land. However, this option is subject to the condition that the farmworkers must genuinely benefit from the arrangement.

The Court finds that the SDOA failed to achieve its purpose. The farmworkers did not receive fair benefits, and the stock distribution did not result in genuine agrarian reform. The PARC's order revoking the SDOA and directing compulsory land distribution is upheld.
